answer: One hourly wharf job bid requires each AI key to complete 1 million sequential modular squarings. Its computation thread starts from a hash of the key and a fresh random beacon pulse. Validators check a delay proof bound to key and hour; missing, invalid or reused proofs get no bid. Absent cross-input shortcuts, n keys need n million squarings. Parallelism reduces elapsed time, not total work. Compute is a recurring expense; hardware is reusable. Sound proofs and unpredictable pulses are essential; faster chips buy cheaper bids, and validator collusion can waive work.
